title: Cluster 03 DRILL: Diseases, Antibiotics, Vaccination and Epidemiology
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 9, Extension Topic A · 10 questions · 87 marks · 32 parts · one mark per minute, so a little under an hour and a half · every question is an actual exam paper question except five parts labelled CONSTRUCTED
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b), that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE; a right answer said confidently moves on.

Every question below is a real exam paper question, except five parts that are labelled [CONSTRUCTED, no real paper question exists] in their own stems and again in their schemes. Those five sit on LOs (j) and (k), where the entire the papers of 901 real Book 9 questions contains exactly two usable stems. Everything else is the paper's own wording, and every edit is recorded in the Sources block.

This cluster carries seven of the eleven outcomes: (e), (f), (g), (h), (i), (j) and (k). It is the biggest of the three by a wide margin, and the bacterial half alone is the papers.

Two outcomes are taught nowhere in your 139 pages. LO (j), the basic reproduction number R0, and LO (k), outbreak, epidemic and pandemic. The cover page promises epidemiology and the sections were never written. 9477 Specimen Paper 1 Question 30 is a real R0 question, so this is not optional. Questions 9 and 10 close both gaps. R0 is quantitative, not just definitional: the syllabus's own Mathematical Requirements on page 25 list "the use of Ro value" beside the Hardy-Weinberg equation and chi-squared, so Question 9 makes you compute with it.

Question 3 is the full-cycle question, thirteen marks running one Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection end to end: a droplet leaves one person, is inhaled by another, defeats the phagocyte that engulfs it, builds a tubercle, sits latent, then ruptures into active contagious disease. Answer (a) to (e) as one story.

Question 4 is the only official structured Book 9 question in existence. 9477 Specimen Paper 2 Question 9, both parts, at its real 7 marks. It was the last question on the paper, and Infectious Diseases was the last thing a candidate met on Paper 1 as well. That timing fact is worth more than most content facts: practise this material tired, at the end of a session, not fresh.

Four real figures, and honesty about the rest. Q2 carries your school's 2025 Paper 2 Figures 5.1 and 5.2, Q3 carries your school's 2024 Paper 2 Figure 10.1, Q4 carries 9477 Specimen Paper 2 Figure 9.1, and Q7 carries RI Prelim 2025 Paper 2 Figure 11.1. Every other figure comes from a paper whose PDF is not in the papers, so the question carries that paper's own printed description rather than a redrawing, and says so on the page.

The Book 4 boundary, so you do not answer the wrong half. Book 4 owns what the pathogen does to its own genome; Book 9 owns what it does to the host. Viral reproductive cycles, antigenic shift and drift, bacterial genetics and antibiotic resistance are all Book 4. No question in this drill sets a viral replication cycle. Q1(b) deliberately reaches across into antigenic drift, because that bridge is the richest in the Book and Specimen P1 Q11 does exactly the same thing: Book 9 framing over a Book 4 answer is this paper's house style.

What the marks reward. Write Mycobacterium tuberculosis in full and correctly, because a scheme states spelling must be correct and rejects the answer "bacteria". Write HIV, never HIV virus. Name the compartment: phagosome, and say no phagolysosome forms, because an examiner names "prevent fusion of lysosomes" and "hide in host cells" as lacking rigour. Write transpeptidase, never peptidyl transferase and never "glycoprotein peptidases". Name the missing target when you say antibiotics do not act on viruses, because a scheme rejects vague mention of cell machinery and notes must state specific organelles. Discuss questions need a stand, and a scheme records "if no stand taken = 0m; if both given = max 1m".

Three errors in your own notes are corrected in the schemes here. Q4(a) carries the correction to printed page 112, which says penicillin blocks the glycoprotein peptidases. Q6 carries the correction to printed page 118, which swaps the smallpox and cowpox virus names. Q7(c) carries the discipline on herd immunity that a scheme enforces where the affected proportion is under one per cent.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required answers and not only duplicated labels. Q1 how a virus destroys the tissue it infects · Q2 how a virus disables the immune system itself, and virulence read off two graphs · Q3 one bacterial infection from droplet to ruptured tubercle · Q4 penicillin, and the specimen's own antibody-against-antibiotic comparison · Q5 the boundary of what antibiotics cannot act on · Q6 the named eradication case at essay scale · Q7 herd immunity read off real vaccination data · Q8 the benefits and risks weighed, with a documented reject list · Q9 R0 defined, applied and computed · Q10 the spread ladder, defined and applied.

Where two questions touch the same clinical fact they need different paragraphs. TB in an AIDS patient appears three times and each time from a different outcome: Q2(a) explains the helper T cell loss under (g), Q3(e) explains the ruptured tubercle under (h), and Q5(b) explains why an antibiotic is prescribed at all under (i). Herd immunity appears in Q6 as part of the smallpox case, in Q7 as a data interpretation, and in Q9(e) as an arithmetic consequence of R0; none of the three schemes credits the same sentence.

No viral replication cycle is set anywhere in this drill. Reproductive cycles of enveloped viruses and retroviruses are Core Idea 2 LO 2(e), antigenic shift and drift are 2(f), bacterial genetics and antibiotic resistance are 2(g), and all four belong to Book 4. Q1(b) reaches into 2(f) deliberately as the Book 9 to Book 4 bridge, and Q5(c) marks the resistance boundary so you do not revise it here.
